# Change the framework

The framework is this repository ([entry file](../../../AGENTS.md), section 9): a change here reaches every project with the next version. Read the one section below that fits, then finish with the common steps.

## A core rule (a line of `core/rules/` with its `rule:` id)

1. A change of the **meaning** of a rule or of a non-negotiable needs the owner's confirmation, recorded in the pull request; ask before you edit. A rewording that keeps the meaning does not.
2. Edit the template in `core/rules/`. The wording stays neutral: no stack, runtime, host or project word (`harness check core` holds it), and a value is cited by its role. Keep the id of the rule; a new rule gets a new stable id, and `tools/lib/entry.test.mjs` lists the ids of every block, so update that list.
3. Say how the rule is held: an adapter that enforces it declares it in the `enforces` of its manifest; a rule nothing checks is judgment. `npm run harness -- sync --local` regenerates the entry file's blocks and the rule-to-check map ([the map](../../../docs/engineering/rule-checks.md)); never edit them by hand.

## A check of the tools (`harness check <name>`)

1. A pure function with a test next to it (`*.test.mjs`) that plants a defect and sees it fail; a seam (the clock, the file system root, the host's command line) is a parameter.
2. Register it in `tools/lib/checks.mjs` (it then runs in `check all`), and add it to the command list of `tools/harness.mjs` and of the README.
3. Name it in the rule-to-check map when it holds a rule, through the `enforces` of an adapter or the project's own rows below the generated block.

## A role of the profile

1. Add the role to `profile/harness-profile.schema.json` with its description and, when a project may omit it, a default or "optional". A role that a template resolves is required of every project that renders the template: **a template that a sync renders with the tools of an older version must use only roles those tools know**, so new behavior comes from new code and not from a new placeholder.
2. Say it in the document of roles (`profile/roles.md`) only when the template can render it for a project that lacks it; add it to the starter answers (`profile/starter.json`) and the bootstrap questions when a new project needs a value.
3. A role that changes the meaning of an existing profile file needs a migration (`migrations/<version>.mjs`, `migrations/README.md`) and a note for the version.

## Every change

1. The change reaches projects through the distributable paths of `framework.json`; write a changelog fragment in `changelog.d/` that says what a project must do about it, and a migration note when it must do something.
2. Tests for every new behavior; run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run docs:check`.
3. The pull request follows the entry file. A change to a contract (design §1.4) or to the meaning of a core rule needs the owner's approval in it, and a major version.
